If you cannot decide now, you will never be able to decide in your entire life.
All of you spend busy days every single day.
I'll say it straight!
To put it bluntly, this is your last chance!
Because a great many people are waiting for me.
This is my mission!

lines.trans: Just now!
I'll buy it! Right now?
Thank you very much for your purchase. There is only now!
See you later.

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Humble counterpart of いる, commonly used in ～ております.
Humble noun form of 待たせる, used in apologies like お待たせしました.

examples.text: 大変お待たせいたしました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for waiting.

examples.text: お待たせしてすみません。

meanings.note: Polite/honorific form of 忙しい with prefix お.

examples.text: お忙しいところすみません。
examples.trans: Sorry to bother you while you're busy.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Short for かもしれない; expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Honorific form of 購入, commonly used by salespeople thanking customers.

examples.text: ご購入ありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your purchase.

examples.text: ご購入を検討しています。

meanings.note: Always pairs with a negative verb; するしかありません means 'have no choice but to do'.

examples.trans: I only have one thousand yen.
There is no choice but to do it.

meanings.note: Compound ichidan verb formed from する + すぎる.

examples.text: 最近働きすぎています。
examples.trans: I've been working too much lately.

examples.text: 心配しすぎないでください。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; most commonly appears in the set expression かもしれない ('might be').

examples.text: 遅れるかもしれません。
本当かもしれませんよ。
examples.trans: It might be true, you know.

meanings.note: Used adverbially or as a noun to mean 'everything' or 'all of them'.

examples.text: すべてうまくいきました。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Mimetic adverb meaning 'clearly' or 'frankly'.

examples.text: はっきり言ってください。
よく聞こえないので、はっきり話してください。
examples.trans: I can't hear well, so please speak clearly.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Formal, polite first-person pronoun used in business and respectful speech.

examples.text: わたくしが担当いたします。
わたくしはそのように考えます。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Wasei-eigo / loanword from 'just now', used emphatically to mean 'right now!'.

examples.text: 決めるならジャストナウです！
examples.trans: If you're going to decide, it's right now!

examples.text: ジャストナウで行動しましょう。

meanings.note: Na-adjective loanword from English 'straight'.

examples.text: ストレートに言いますね。
彼はストレートな性格です。

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'miracle'.
Loanword compound from English 'last chance'.

examples.text: これがラストチャンスです！
ラストチャンスを逃さないでください。
examples.trans: Please don't miss your last chance.

meanings.note: Used as a noun or adverbially to mean 'for life / forever'.

examples.trans: I will never forget it for the rest of my life.

examples.text: これは一生の思い出です。

meanings.note: Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Refers to a solemn task or purpose one is meant to fulfill.

examples.text: 重要な使命を果たしました。

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Noun derived from 出会う (to meet/encounter).

examples.text: 人との出会いを大切にしています。
素晴らしい出会いがありました。

meanings.en: a great number of people; crowd
meanings.note: Refers to a large number of people (read おおぜい).

examples.text: 大勢の人が集まりました。
examples.trans: A large crowd of people gathered.

examples.text: 大勢の前で話すのは緊張します。
examples.trans: Speaking in front of many people makes me nervous.

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.note: Literary/emphatic plural of 日, meaning 'every day / daily life'.

examples.text: 忙しい日々を過ごしています。

meanings.note: Everyday noun for time on the clock or a dedicated stretch of time.

examples.text: まだ少し時間があります。
examples.trans: There is still a little time.

examples.text: 楽しい時間をありがとう。
examples.trans: Thank you for the fun time.

meanings.note: Temporal noun used adverbially without a particle.

examples.text: 毎日英語を勉強しています。

examples.trans: You're busy every day, aren't you?

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; potential form 決められる means 'can decide'.

examples.text: まだ何も決めていません。
今決められないなら、後で考えましょう。
examples.trans: If you can't decide now, let's think about it later.

meanings.en: justification (申し訳ございません = no excuse / deeply sorry)
meanings.note: Paired with ございません or ありません for formal apologies.

examples.text: 遅れて申し訳ございません。
examples.trans: I am deeply sorry for being late.

examples.text: 大変申し訳ありませんでした。

meanings.note: Polite/honorific plural pronoun for addressing an audience or group.

examples.text: 皆様のご健康をお祈りします。

meanings.note: Verbal noun; 約束する means 'to promise'.

examples.text: 約束の時間に遅れました。
examples.trans: I was late for the appointment time.

meanings.note: 買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective describing either late timing or slow speed.

examples.text: 今日は帰りが遅いです。
この電車は少し遅いですね。
examples.trans: This train is a little slow, isn't it?

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; 時間が過ぎる means 'time passes / it's past the time'.

examples.text: 約束の時間が過ぎています。
examples.trans: We are past the appointment time.

examples.text: 夏休みがすぐに過ぎました。

meanings.note: Transitive godan verb.

examples.text: 週末は家でゆっくり過ごしました。
examples.trans: I spent the weekend relaxing at home.

examples.text: 毎日忙しい日々を過ごしています。
examples.trans: I spend busy days every day.
